probes.question: You know 'If P, then Q' and that P is true. What follows?
options: P and Q are the same

probes.question: True or false: 'If an animal is a dog, it has four legs. My cat has four legs. So my cat is a dog' is valid reasoning.

image.alt: A wet cobblestone street at night glistening with reflected lights after rain.

body.claim: From 'if P then Q' and 'Q', you cannot conclude P.
body.why: 'If P then Q' plus 'P' lets you conclude Q: that is valid reasoning (modus ponens). Flipping it is the fallacy called affirming the consequent. If an animal is a dog, it has four legs; my cat has four legs; so my cat is a dog. Many other causes can lead to the same Q.
